skill.name: gh-address-comments
skill.description: Help address review/issue comments on the open GitHub PR for the current branch using gh CLI; verify gh auth first and prompt the user to authenticate if not logged in.
skill.summary: Guides developers through GitHub PR comment triage and selected fixes with the gh CLI.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are confirmed because the skill directs agents to use the GitHub CLI with authenticated network access. The audit also found high-risk permission escalation language that tells agents to use elevated network access and sandbox_permissions=require_escalated. No evidence found of hidden code or data exfiltration in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that tell agents to use elevated network access or sandbox_permissions=require_escalated. Let the host tool policy request user approval when needed.
Request only the minimum gh scopes needed for PR review work. Avoid workflow scope unless workflow operations are required.
Document exact gh commands and require user confirmation before any command that writes comments, changes branches, or modifies remote state.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line instructs agents to run gh commands with elevated network access. Although the backticks are Markdown formatting, the skill creates a real authenticated external command surface.

The line directs gh authentication checks, asks for repo and workflow scopes, and tells agents to rerun with sandbox_permissions=require_escalated. This is a clear external command and permission escalation risk.
The line instructs users to run gh auth login and retry on failures, which involves credentials and networked GitHub access. This is a legitimate workflow step but still a real external command risk.

content.value_statement: Review comments often scatter across GitHub threads. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to inspect, summarize, and fix selected PR feedback.
actual_capabilities: Finds the open GitHub PR for the current branch.
Checks whether the gh CLI is authenticated before PR work.
Uses a comment fetch workflow to list review threads and comments.
Numbers comments and summarizes the likely fix for each item.
Asks the user which comments should be addressed before applying fixes.
Prompts for GitHub reauthentication when gh auth or rate limits fail.
limitations: Requires the gh CLI, network access, and repository permissions.
References scripts/fetch_comments.py, but that helper is not included in this skill package.
Does not decide which comments to fix without user selection.
Cannot bypass GitHub branch protections or repository access limits.

use_cases.title: Triage Review Threads
use_cases.description: Summarize unresolved PR comments so the developer can choose which feedback to address first.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Small PRs
use_cases.description: Apply selected fixes from reviewer comments while keeping the workflow centered on explicit user choices.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Organize comment status and draft concise replies after accepted feedback has been addressed.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect PR Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments to inspect the open PR on this branch. Summarize each review thread and ask me which ones to address.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Selected Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments to address comments 2 and 4. Make the smallest code changes and show what changed before any write action.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Review Replies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments to inspect unresolved review threads, apply confirmed fixes, and draft concise replies for each resolved comment.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Guarded Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-address-comments to triage the PR, identify risky comments, ask for confirmation on write actions, and prepare a final verification checklist.

output_examples.input: Inspect my open PR and summarize unresolved comments.
output: Thread 1 asks for a clearer validation message.
Thread 2 requests a test for the error path.
Thread 3 asks whether the old option should remain supported.

output_examples.input: Address comment 2 and prepare a response.
output_examples.output: The selected feedback was addressed with a focused test update. Suggested reply: Updated the error-path coverage and verified the previous behavior.

output_examples.input: List comments that need my decision before changes.
output: One comment needs a product decision before implementation.
Two comments look safe to fix directly after your confirmation.
No branch protection or merge status changes were attempted.

best_practices: Confirm the target PR before running write operations.
Review requested GitHub scopes before authentication.
Ask the user to select comments before applying fixes.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad gh commands before confirming the repository and branch.
Do not request workflow scope unless workflow changes are required.
Do not auto-fix every comment without user selection.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects gh CLI authentication before it can inspect PR comments or related review data.

faq.question: Can it work without the gh CLI?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow depends on gh commands and repository access through GitHub.

faq.question: Will it fix every reviewer comment automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks the user which numbered comments should be addressed before applying fixes.

faq.question: Does it include the comment fetching script?
faq.answer: No. The skill references scripts/fetch_comments.py, but the audited package only contains SKILL.md.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: It can be used only when the authenticated GitHub account has the required repository permissions.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
